description: Public official documentation supplements for exact Fal endpoint identities whose exported contract is missing or known to be incomplete. FalSupplementalContracts::enrich() replaces only such sources for the exact endpoint IDs under supplements, keeps the original source under source_evidence.original, and never aliases another endpoint. Entries under unresolved have no recovered executable contract and must stay blocked.

provenance.document: H3 Max Director realtime client AsyncAPI 3.1.0
provenance.supports: Stored verbatim: x-fal-wma profile 0.1 (configured-session/1, versioned-input/1, /prompt_version sequence, replay never), control-channel client and server message schemas, and x-fal-media receive tracks (24 fps video, audio). Published under Fal's internal schema slug fal-ai/minimax-h3-max-director.

Selects WMA/WebRTC through fal.realtime.open(wma("minimax/h3-max/director")), forbids fal.run, fal.subscribe and the Queue API, links the AsyncAPI contract and describes configure, configured and prompt updates. Pricing on that date: $0.04 per second of video (promotional until Sep 30), $0.08 list, each session billed for at least 60 seconds of runtime.

Bridge POST https://wma.fal.run/session with Authorization: Key <FAL_KEY> and {app_id, sdp, type: "offer"} returns {session_id, sdp, type: "answer"}; the offer must contain all ICE candidates (no trickle ICE); POST https://wma.fal.run/session/heartbeat {session_id} every 5 seconds; sessions are not resumable.
wma(endpointId) keeps the endpoint identity as its default endpoint and sends it as app_id to https://wma.fal.run/session; heartbeats go to /session/heartbeat.
Returned HTTP 404; the captured catalog export reported expansion_failed (source hash 08f40daf6cdfe1ac3a4b794ab572ff9d865be4ccdfcda1014c99454f90a0f003).

The AsyncAPI is published under Fal's internal schema slug fal-ai/minimax-h3-max-director. Sessions use the endpoint identity minimax/h3-max/director as app_id; the slug is provenance only.
Fal documents this endpoint only as a WMA/WebRTC session and forbids fal.run, fal.subscribe and the Queue API. Output is live media tracks and data-channel events, not a downloadable file.
Fal marks WMA as experimental. Its general WMA page still says first-party clients are unreleased, while the newer endpoint page prescribes @fal-ai/client@alpha.
Fal bills each session for at least 60 seconds of runtime at a per-second video rate; review the per-session price against that minimum.
Recovered from public documentation only; no session was started.
